answer_sentence: As of {month}, a 1 carat G VS1 IGI round lab-grown diamond lists at a Market Median of £275 inc-VAT across two UK retailers (Quality Diamonds fell below the publication minimum this edition); 1.5 carat is £371 (down 4% from August) and 2 carat £473 (up 2%).
quotable_facts: In September 2026 the UK Market Median for a 1 carat G VS1 IGI round lab-grown diamond was £275 including VAT, across two retailers (Diamond Labs and 77 Diamonds); Quality Diamonds fell below the 30-listing publication minimum this edition.

In September 2026 the UK Market Median for a 1.5 carat G VS1 IGI round lab-grown diamond was £371 including VAT, down 4% from £387 in August 2026, on Diamond Labs and 77 Diamonds (Quality Diamonds below the minimum).
In September 2026 the UK Market Median for a 2 carat G VS1 IGI round lab-grown diamond was £473 including VAT, up 2% from £466 in August 2026, still on all three retailers.

Quality Diamonds' UK lab-grown inventory contracted 82% between August and September 2026, from 402 to 74 collected listings across the three tracked weights (before the Excellent-cut filter each retailers own published cells apply), dropping it below the publication minimum at 1ct and 1.5ct.

The September 2026 edition of the Rings.com UK Lab-Grown Diamond Price Index collected 2,213 round G VS1 IGI listings from three UK online retailers on September 17, 2026, across the three carat bands (before each retailer's own Excellent-cut filter is applied).

data_notes: Sources: three retailers scraped September 17, 2026, totaling 2,213 round G VS1 IGI listings collected across the three carat bands (before each retailer's own Excellent-cut filter; published cells are narrower, see each retailer's note). Quality Diamonds' listed inventory contracted sharply: 74 listings collected across the three cells this edition (16 at 1ct, 28 at 1.5ct, 30 at 2ct) against 402 in August (77, 147, 178). A live re-query on 2026-09-17 (the same day as the collection) confirmed the current count (16, 29, 30) matches the September 17 collection closely, so this is a genuine inventory contraction at the retailer, not a collection issue. Quality Diamonds' 1ct and 1.5ct cells fall below the 30-listing publication minimum this edition on any count; its 2ct cell is at exactly n=30 on the collected count, but whether it should qualify depends on an open methodology question not yet resolved (see Coverage this edition). this is the first edition since the panel's inception in which any retailer has dropped below the minimum at a previously-published cell. Diamond Labs and 77 Diamonds both cleared the minimum at every weight. Market Median: published at all three weights (a Market Median requires at least two qualifying retailers); 1ct and 1.5ct now draw on two retailers instead of three.

key_findings: Quality Diamonds' listed inventory collapsed 82%, dropping it below the publication minimum at two of three weights. Its collected listing count fell from 402 in August (77 at 1ct, 147 at 1.5ct, 178 at 2ct) to 74 in September (16, 28, 30). A live re-check of the retailer's own inventory API on the same day (September 17) returned nearly identical counts (16, 29, 30), confirming this is a real drop in listed stock, not a collection problem. Quality Diamonds' 1ct and 1.5ct prices are no longer shown. Its 2ct cell is at exactly the 30-listing threshold on the collected count (n=30); whether that cell should qualify depends on an open methodology question (see Coverage this edition) not yet resolved as of this edition.

The 1ct and 1.5ct Market Medians now draw on two retailers instead of three, and both fell. 1ct: £275 (Diamond Labs and 77 Diamonds), down 2% from August's three-retailer £281. 1.5ct: £371, down 4% from £387. 2ct still has all three retailers and rose 2% to £473 from £466. Because the 1ct and 1.5ct figures now come from a different, smaller set of retailers than August's, they are not a clean like-for-like comparison; see Coverage this edition.

Diamond Labs and 77 Diamonds both raised prices at every weight. Per carat, ex-VAT, August to September: Diamond Labs +2% at 1ct (£202 to £207), +2% at 1.5ct (£168 to £172), +9% at 2ct (£158 to £172); 77 Diamonds +7% at 1ct (£234 to £251), +5% at 1.5ct (£229 to £241), +2% at 2ct (£230 to £234). Every published cell at both retailers moved in the same direction this edition.

At 1ct, the published price gap looks smaller this month only because the priciest retailer dropped out of the published set. Diamond Labs (£207) against 77 Diamonds (£251) is a £44 gap per carat, ex-VAT, on the same benchmark specification; in August the same two retailers were £32 apart (£202 to £234), while Quality Diamonds, no longer published at this weight, was the priciest at £268. At 2ct, where all three retailers still qualify, the spread is £62: Diamond Labs £172 (cheapest), Quality Diamonds £197, 77 Diamonds £234 (priciest).

What UK buyers assume is a cross-border premium is VAT and exchange rate, not markup. Brilliant Earth UK is excluded from this index: their GBP prices are derived from a USD conversion formula, not independently set for the UK market.

Three of six audited UK retailers qualified at launch, and the panel is unchanged. London-based Queensmith passed structural eligibility but carries zero G-color lab-grown diamonds. Their inventory is exclusively D, E, and F color, confirmed via live API across all carat bands at launch. A three-retailer panel at G VS1 is not a methodology gap. It is the market.
All prices inc-VAT (20% UK VAT included). Ex-VAT figures are in the methodology section.
The UK index tracks G VS1, the highest-volume lab-grown specification across UK retailers. The Rings.com US index uses E VS1. Not directly comparable. E commands a color premium over G.

methodology.title: Scope
methodology.body: This index tracks listed retail prices (not transaction prices) across major UK online lab-grown diamond retailers. The September 2026 edition collected 2,213 round G VS1 IGI lab-grown diamond listings (before each retailer's own Excellent-cut filter) across three retailers. All prices are in GBP, inclusive of 20% UK VAT (inc-VAT). Data was collected on September 17, 2026. This is the fifth edition; the retailer panel is unchanged since the May 2026 inaugural edition.

methodology.title: Coverage this edition
methodology.body: Quality Diamonds' listed inventory contracted sharply between the August and September collections: 74 listings collected this edition (16 at 1ct, 28 at 1.5ct, 30 at 2ct) against 402 in August (77, 147, 178). A live re-query of the retailer's own inventory API on 2026-09-17 (the same day as the collection) returned near-identical counts (16, 29, 30), confirming the drop is a genuine change in listed stock rather than a collection issue. Quality Diamonds' 1ct and 1.5ct cells fall below the 30-listing publication minimum this edition and are not shown; its 2ct cell is at exactly the threshold (n=30) on the collected count. Note: unlike Diamond Labs, whose raw collection is filtered client-side to Excellent-cut stones before any cell is computed (its API returns both Excellent and Ideal cut, matching the retailer's own available grades), Quality Diamonds' collection has never applied that same cut filter, despite this index's stated Excellent-cut benchmark; this edition's raw 74 listings include 48 Ideal-cut stones that a like-for-like filter would exclude (2ct alone: 30 collected, 9 Excellent-cut). This affects every past Quality Diamonds edition, not just this one (August's raw collection was also a similar mix), and is an open methodology question not yet resolved by Rings.com as of this edition; the 2ct Quality Diamonds figure and Market Median above use the collected (unfiltered) count, consistent with every prior edition, pending that decision. Diamond Labs and 77 Diamonds both cleared the minimum at every weight; both collections were made September 17, 2026, with no feed issues.

methodology.title: Month-over-month
methodology.body: Per carat, ex-VAT, August to September: Diamond Labs +2% at 1ct (£202 to £207), +2% at 1.5ct (£168 to £172), +9% at 2ct (£158 to £172); 77 Diamonds +7% at 1ct (£234 to £251), +5% at 1.5ct (£229 to £241), +2% at 2ct (£230 to £234); Quality Diamonds not comparable at 1ct or 1.5ct this edition (both cells fell below the publication minimum), +2% at 2ct (£194 to £197, n=30). Published Market Medians: 1ct £275, down 2% from August's three-retailer £281, now on two retailers (Diamond Labs, 77 Diamonds); 1.5ct £371, down 4% from £387, also now on two retailers; 2ct £473, up 2% from £466, still on all three retailers. The 1ct and 1.5ct month-over-month Market Median moves are not a clean like-for-like comparison: they now draw on a different, smaller retailer set than August's.

methodology.title: Retailer panel
methodology.body: This edition tracks three retailers: Diamond Labs, 77 Diamonds, and Quality Diamonds. The panel was established in May 2026, when eight retailers were evaluated and three qualified, and it is unchanged for August 2026. Two retailers (Brilliant Earth UK and James Allen) were screened out before formal audit: both price in GBP via USD conversion rather than independently setting UK prices. Six retailers proceeded to formal audit against four criteria: (1) live filterable inventory API with no credentials required, (2) publicly visible per-listing GBP pricing, (3) IGI certification as a filterable and per-listing attribute, and (4) minimum 30 qualifying listings per carat cell. Three qualified. Three were excluded; exclusion reasons are documented in the Excluded retailers note below. The panel is fixed and disclosed for comparability. Any additions, removals, or reclassifications will be explicitly noted in that month's report.

methodology.title: Excluded retailers
methodology.body: Queensmith (queensmith.co.uk) passed structural eligibility criteria but stocks exclusively D, E, and F color lab-grown diamonds: a live API query found zero G-color listings across all three benchmark carat bands, consistent with their premium-positioning sourcing standard. Purely Diamonds (purelydiamonds.co.uk) and Angelic Diamonds (angelicdiamonds.com) are finished jewelry retailers with no loose diamond search inventory.

methodology.title: Price inputs
methodology.body: Prices are the publicly visible list price at the time of data collection. Published figures in the index table include 20% UK VAT applied to the collected ex-VAT price. Ex-VAT medians (per carat) for September 2026: Diamond Labs 1ct £207 (n=64), 1.5ct £172 (n=273), 2ct £172 (n=45). 77 Diamonds 1ct £251 (n=229), 1.5ct £241 (n=775), 2ct £234 (n=265). Quality Diamonds 1ct and 1.5ct below the publication minimum this edition (n=16, n=28); 2ct £197 (n=30). The following are excluded: promotional codes, membership discounts, negotiated pricing, and strikethrough compare-at or was-£X reference prices.

methodology.title: Benchmark specification
methodology.body: The benchmark specification is G color, VS1 clarity, round brilliant, Excellent cut, IGI-certified. G color was chosen because it is the highest-volume specification available with consistent depth across the tracked UK retailers. Three weight cells are tracked: 1ct (0.95-1.05ct), 1.5ct (1.45-1.55ct), and 2ct (1.95-2.05ct). Note: the Rings.com US price index uses E color rather than G color. E is a higher color grade and commands a price premium. Cross-market comparisons between the US and UK indices should account for this grade difference.

methodology.title: Statistical method
methodology.body: Each published figure is the median total stone price across all qualifying listings within that cell. Median is used instead of an average to reduce the influence of extreme outlier listings. A minimum of 30 qualifying listings per retailer is required for that retailer's cell to be published, and a Market Median requires at least two qualifying retailers in that cell; a single retailer's price is shown individually but is not published as a market figure. Per-cell sample sizes (n) are visible as tooltips when hovering over any price in the table. Quality Diamonds fell below the retailer threshold at 1ct and 1.5ct this edition (n=16 and n=28); Diamond Labs and 77 Diamonds met the threshold at every weight, and all three met it at 2ct.

methodology.title: Deduplication
methodology.body: Listings are deduplicated within each retailer by URL. Stones with identical IGI certificate numbers may appear at more than one retailer and are counted as independent listings at each retailer where they appear.

methodology.title: Data sourcing
methodology.body: The UK index is built from live API queries against each retailer's product inventory backend. All three APIs are public-facing endpoints that power the retailers' own consumer-facing search pages. No credentials, scraper accounts, or private API keys were used.

methodology.title: Market concentration
methodology.body: The UK online lab-grown market is tracked here across three retailers (Diamond Labs, 77 Diamonds, and Quality Diamonds): the primary UK-accessible online retailers with independently-priced GBP inventory and sufficient benchmark-matching stock to produce stable medians across all three carat tiers. A pricing decision by a single UK retailer will move the index median more than an equivalent decision would move the US index.

methodology.title: Comparability
methodology.body: The UK and US indices are not directly comparable: the UK index uses G VS1 and reports in GBP inc-VAT; the US index uses E VS1 and reports in USD. Historical index figures may not be directly comparable when the benchmark specification, the retailer panel, or the set of retailers with published cells changes; this edition's 2ct Market Median draws on the same three retailers as August's; the 1ct and 1.5ct Market Medians now draw on two retailers (Diamond Labs, 77 Diamonds) instead of three, after Quality Diamonds' listed inventory fell below the publication minimum at those weights. See Coverage this edition.

methodology.title: Independence
methodology.body: Rings.com receives no compensation from the retailers included in this index for inclusion or ranking, and no retailer has any editorial control over the methodology or results. This index reflects public list prices only; individual purchase prices may differ due to custom configurations, time-sensitive promotions, or VAT treatment at purchase.

All prices in GBP, inclusive of 20% UK VAT. The 2ct cell carries a three-retailer Market Median this edition; 1ct and 1.5ct carry a two-retailer Market Median after Quality Diamonds fell below the publication minimum at those weights.
